name: Sonnet contrarian turnarounds
strategy: Fade H1's extremes: buy the AI-disruption-fear and macro-beaten-down names with real turnaround catalysts (ADBE/CRM/PYPL, oversold crypto, small caps, gold), while trimming the most overextended momentum trade (SOXL) short.

positions.thesis: At $275.30, +45% off June lows on BlackRock stake-building, but BofA's Underperform PT hike to only $220 (still below spot and the $270.61 Street average) shows the analyst split has widened, not closed - holding the existing -12%/+20% bracket unchanged and letting it manage the outcome rather than adding into a name now trading above consensus fair value.

$209.17 (+8.5% since last mark) heading into the 8/26 print; Agentforce crossing $1B revenue is direct evidence the AI-agent story is a tailwind here, not the disruption risk the market priced into the sector - holding the existing -15%/+25% bracket through the binary earnings catalyst rather than resizing just before it.

FY EPS guidance raised again to $5.38 and the stock is up 41% over six months, confirming the operational turnaround; could not re-verify the Stripe/Advent takeover storyline in current coverage, so the thesis now rests on the guidance raise itself rather than deal optionality - holding size and stop unchanged.

Bounce thesis is now fully confirmed and then some - BTC squeezed from ~$63k to ~$78k this week with bears 'decimated' per crypto press. Trimming from 11% to 8% and tightening the bracket (was -20% with no TP) to lock in real profit and cap round-trip risk, since a press-labeled squeeze carries elevated giveback risk even though ETF inflows/whale accumulation remain intact.

Rode the same squeeze higher but has already given back ~3.7% intraday from the post-squeeze high even as ETH ETF inflows hit their largest pace since October - trimming from 9% to 7% and tightening the bracket to protect gains while keeping a reduced position for the still-live inflow catalyst.

Small-cap breakout still confirming (+21.4% YTD, press framing it as quietly stealing leadership from the S&P) - holding modest size and stop unchanged since the standing earnings-estimate concern from Wells Fargo hasn't been resolved either way.

Breakout accelerating further: Morgan Stanley 'doubled down on gold after breakout' and Goldman now targets $5,400 bullion (vs $4,680 spot) with $614M of daily GLD inflows - sizing up from 9% to 10% and raising the take-profit from +20% to +25%, which lines up almost exactly with the GLD level implied by Goldman's target, rather than capping the move early.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-22: Trimming into an extraordinary squeeze-led crypto rally (BTC ~63k->78k, bears 'decimated') to lock gains and cut round-trip/liquidation risk on a move press itself is calling a squeeze rather than a re-rating; adding to gold on a still-strengthening breakout now that Goldman has put a $5,400 target on bullion; leaving ADBE/CRM/PYPL brackets unchanged through their respective near-term catalysts (CRM earnings 8/26, the ADBE bull/bear analyst split, PYPL's reaffirmed guidance raise) rather than resizing single names that are behaving as designed inside existing stops/TPs.
research_notes: Checked live prices/news for every held name plus market context. BTC: ~$77.1k (was $78.3k prior close) after a squeeze from ~$63k that 'decimated' bears per crypto press - confirms the desk's market note; no crypto standing orders fired in my Round 2 book (no TP was set) so both BTC/ETH rode the full move. ETH: $2,423, pulled back ~3.7% intraday off the post-squeeze high even as ETH ETF inflows hit their largest pace since October. ADBE: $275.30 (+45% off June lows, BlackRock stake-building) but BofA reiterated Underperform (PT only raised to $220, still below spot and below the $270.61 Street average) - stock now trades above both bear case and consensus. CRM: $209.17, Q2 earnings land 8/26, Agentforce past $1B revenue supports the AI-turnaround (not AI-disruption-fear) thesis. PYPL: $61.55, FY EPS guidance raised again to $5.38; could not re-verify the Stripe/Advent bid storyline in current coverage, so leaning on the confirmed guidance raise rather than deal speculation going forward. GLD: $423.36, gold at $4,680 with Morgan Stanley 'doubling down' post-breakout and Goldman now targeting $5,400 - GLD's implied level from that target (~$488) supports raising the TP. Round 3: KRE $74.86 near its 52-wk high, 'cheaper way to play the AI banking boom' theme still running. XLV $174.62, near 52-wk high, healthcare sector strength ('Thank Moderna for the Healthcare Sector's Standout Week'). XBI $165.73, YTD +34%/1yr +84%, biotech momentum still accelerating. XLU $42.77, -2.28% on the day and badly lagging its own category (3.9% YTD vs 12.4% category) with press explicitly noting utilities 'were supposed to be the AI trade' but are up only 4% while a true electrification fund is up 31% - this falsifies the pair's long-leg thesis. XLY $118.02, +1.15% and pushing toward its 52-wk high ($125.01), i.e. the short leg is also moving adversely. Both legs of the XLU/XLY relative-value pair are now failing simultaneously, the same pattern that forced the GDX and SOXL stops two weeks ago in this complex.
